notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.5.15.3 SR3: "All numeric literals in a VALUE clause of an item must have a value which is within the range of values indicated by the PICTURE clause, and must not have a value which would require truncation of nonzero digits. Nonnumeric literals in a VALUE clause of an item must not exceed the size indicated by the PICTURE clause." Implemented at 85 for a data item: every VALUE literal passes ScreenValueLiteral; ValidateNumericValue refuses a numeric literal with a nonzero digit outside the PICTURE's digit positions on either side (COBOL1625), and ValidateValueCategory refuses a nonnumeric literal longer than the size ValueSubject.ForElementary takes from the PICTURE, for alphabetic, alphanumeric and alphanumeric edited items (COBOL1740) and for numeric edited items (COBOL1570); neither arm has an edition test. Implemented for the numeric literals of a condition-name too (BindCondition sends each literal and both ends of a THRU range through the same funnel). Not implemented at 85: the nonnumeric literal of a condition-name. BindCondition passes ValueSubject.ForConditionName, which carries no size, so the size sentence never reaches it. That choice was derived from the 2023 words "of an elementary item" and "an explicit PICTURE clause" (§2023:13.18.63.3 SR4); the 1985 sentence has neither word. The 1985 rule reaches the condition-name entry: its first sentence speaks of "All numeric literals in a VALUE clause", and only the condition-name format takes more than one literal; §1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1 a says the same way "all literals in the VALUE clause must be numeric"; and §1985:VI.5.15.5 GR1 gives the entry its PICTURE: "The characteristics of a condition-name are implicitly those of its conditional variable." The compiler already reads the first sentence that way at 85 (88 NC VALUE 123 on PIC 99 is COBOL1625), and both sentences use the same words, "in a VALUE clause of an item". Probed at --std 85: refused are 123 in PIC 9(2), 1.25 in 9V9, 12.5 in 9(2), 1230 in 99PP, .012 in PP99, 12345 in 9(4) COMP, 10000 in 9(4) BINARY, -1000 in S9(3) PACKED-DECIMAL, -100 in S99, "ABC" in X(2), A(2) and X(2) JUSTIFIED, "ABCD" in XBX, "1234" in ZZ9, "12/345" in 99/99, oversize literals on table elements, and 88 values 123, 1 THRU 100 and 1.5 on PIC 99; accepted are 012, 1.20, 1200, .0012, 0012.00, -99, a shorter nonnumeric literal and ALL "ABC" in X(2); accepted and not legal are 88 VALUE "cd" on PIC X, 88 VALUE "a" THRU "zz" on PIC X and 88 VALUE "1234" on PIC ZZ9. The witness is PIC ZZ9 VALUE "1234", refused with COBOL1570.

next.reason: The numeric part is kept: §2023:13.18.63.3 SR2 'permissible values within the range indicated by the PICTURE clause ... without truncation of leading or trailing nonzero digits' (its float exceptions cover usages 1985 lacks), and §2023:13.18.63.3 SR6 extends no-truncation to numeric literals for numeric-edited items. The nonnumeric size limit is kept by §2023:13.18.63.3 SR4 only for alphabetic, alphanumeric and alphanumeric-edited items. 1985 limits a nonnumeric literal for ANY item, and numeric edited items take only nonnumeric literals there (§1985:VI.5.15.4 GR1b). 2023 states no size limit for an alphanumeric literal in a numeric-edited item: §2023:13.18.63.3 SR7 constrains only its class. An oversize literal for a numeric-edited item, refused in 1985, is refused by no 2023 rule.
